newsitem.title: India: Doctors hopeful Mother Teresa will recover.
newsitem.headline: Doctors hopeful Mother Teresa will recover.

text.p: Mother Teresa said her prayers and ate lunch sitting in a chair on Monday, and doctors said they were optimistic the 86-year-old nun would recover from her third heart surgery in five years.

"She is stable and we are very optimistic about her recovery," U.S. doctor Patricia Aubanel, a member of the medical team treating the Roman Catholic missionary, told reporters at Calcutta's B.M. Birla Heart Research Centre.
Doctors said Mother Teresa was better after a bad weekend fighting a long-standing lung problem and poor kidneys while recovering from surgery to clear blocked arteries.
"Today she is better than yesterday," the panel of doctors treating the legendary missionary at the heart clinic said in a late night medical bulletin.
The bulletin, read to reporters by a heart clinic official shortly after 10 p.m. (1630 GMT), said Mother Teresa had shown no change since the previous bulletin issued in the afternoon.
"Mother Teresa's condition has remained unchanged since the last bulletin," the statement said.
Doctors said she ate some soup and chicken sandwiches at 9.30 p.m. (1600 GMT) before going to bed.
"Now she is sleeping," the bulletin added.

Mother Teresa, considered by many a living saint for her devotion to the poor, destitute and dying, had surgery on Friday to clear two blocked coronary arteries. She is also suffering kidney and lung problems as well as pneumonia.
"Mother is still not out of danger, and complications may still happen -- but doctors this morning are optimistic," the doctors said in an earlier bulletin.

"She is alert, cooperative with doctors, accepting her treatment," the afternoon bulletin said. "She had lunch sitting on the chair. This afternoon she is sleeping peacefully. Doctors continue to be optimistic."

A.K. Chatterjee, administrator of the heart clinic, said Mother Teresa again arose from bed in the early evening. "She just got up from bed and is having some physiotherapy exercises," he said without elaborating.
Aubanel said doctors were now concentrating on Mother Teresa's kidney and lung problems.
The hospital said that on Sunday doctors were concerned that Mother Teresa's chronic lung disease, bronchial pneumonia and poor kidneys might set back her recovery.
"Continuous monitoring and support are being given so that other organs do not deteriorate while the heart is recovering," the hospital said in a medical bulletin earlier on Monday.

D.P. Shetty, chief of the medical team treating her, said on Sunday that Mother Teresa's heart pacemaker, fitted in 1989, had been reprogrammed to increase the flow of blood and help her kidneys function better.
Asked when Mother Teresa might be allowed to return to her Missionaries of Charity religious order, Aubanel said: "It's too early to say when she will be released."
Vice-President Kocheril Raman Narayanan and the governor of West Bengal state, K.V. Raghunath Reddy visited the 1979 Nobel Peace Prize winner briefly.

Mother Teresa told Aubanel to work hard, and the U.S. doctor replied that the renowned nun also had to work hard to get well, the bulletin said. "That is my duty, so I will do," it quoted Mother Teresa as saying.
She has undergone heart surgery twice -- in the United States in 1991 and at the Birla centre in 1993.
Mother Teresa, born of Albanian parents as Agnes Gonxhe Bojaxhi, was moved to the Birla clinic last Tuesday after entering the nearby Woodlands Nursing Home on November 22.
Nuns at the Calcutta headquarters of Missionaries of Charity, founded by Mother Teresa in 1949 and now with about 4,500 nuns in some 80 countries, have held prayers for her recovery.
